key_insight: The model predicts Alzheimer’s disease progression over time while also estimating how uncertain each future forecast is, instead of giving only a single next-step diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: This could help research teams better anticipate likely disease trajectories and identify cases where forecasts are less reliable, especially around MCI-to-dementia transitions.
method: Temporal Fusion Transformer encoder with CORAL ordinal diagnosis output
Autoregressive Mixture Density Network for 5-year trajectories of diagnosis, CDR-SB, MMSE orientation, and hippocampal volume
Decomposed uncertainty estimation using analytic mixture variance plus a five-member bootstrap ensemble
evidence_signal: On ADNI, the model outperformed linear, recurrent, and transformer baselines for next-visit diagnosis prediction, with near-nominal 90% credible interval coverage for generated trajectories and external testing on OASIS-3.
watch_item: Performance and uncertainty estimates may shift outside the datasets studied, so external validation and careful monitoring are needed before practical use.
paper_title: Uncertainty-Aware Longitudinal Forecasting of Alzheimer's Disease Progression Using Deep Learning
